stories.headline: Xi criticizes Takaichi's rearmament push to Trump at Beijing summit; Trump reportedly defends her
stories.summary: At the US-China summit in Beijing earlier in May, Chinese President Xi Jinping criticized Japanese PM Takaichi over her remilitarization drive and Taiwan stance, urging Trump not to support her or Taiwanese President Lai. Multiple outlets citing government sources report Trump responded by defending Takaichi, and separately that he called her first after the summit concluded. The exchange has been reported via Yomiuri Shimbun and the Financial Times.

stories.headline: Quad foreign ministers convene in New Delhi on May 26; Japan's Motegi reaffirms grouping's relevance
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of the US, Japan, Australia, and India are meeting in New Delhi on May 26, with US Secretary of State Rubio making his first India visit. Japan's FM Motegi confirmed attendance and publicly declared the Quad a 'vital framework,' pushing back on questions about its diminishing relevance following the Trump-Xi summit. The meeting agenda centers on Indo-Pacific security, the West Asia crisis fallout, and a potential leaders' summit.

stories.headline: LDP formally approves AI-blockchain financial infrastructure roadmap with yen stablecoins and tokenized deposits
stories.summary: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party formally approved a policy proposal titled 'Next-Generation AI & Onchain Finance Concept,' drafted by a project team led by lawmaker Seiji Kihara. The proposal outlines a five-year roadmap for 24/7 automated financial infrastructure using blockchain, yen stablecoins, tokenized bank deposits, and AI-driven payments, with the FSA designated as the oversight body. Multiple crypto/fintech outlets covered the story extensively.

stories.headline: Takaichi orders supplementary budget for energy shock relief amid Middle East crisis
stories.summary: PM Takaichi reversed her earlier position and called on Finance Minister Katayama to compile a supplementary budget of roughly ¥3 trillion to address surging energy costs driven by the Hormuz Strait closure and Middle East war. Debates center on the size, bond issuance, and whether gasoline, electricity, and food consumption tax subsidies should be extended. The BOJ-government relationship and fiscal credibility are running themes.

stories.headline: China cuts Japan's rare earth supply for four months; Japan trade minister makes first brief ministerial contact
stories.summary: China has halted exports of several heavy rare earths including dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium to Japan for at least four months, coinciding with the diplomatic dispute over Taiwan. Separately, Japan's trade minister Akazawa had a brief informal conversation with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang on May 23, described as the first ministerial-level face-to-face contact since the row began. Japan's ambassador in Beijing is working toward a Takaichi-Xi summit at APEC.

stories.headline: LDP launches 200-member 'National Power Research Group' to back Takaichi's security and economic agenda
stories.summary: A new cross-factional LDP group, the Kokuryoku Kenkyukai (National Strength Study Group), was launched on May 22 with more than 200 lawmakers — roughly 83% of LDP members — joining at its inaugural meeting. Former PM Taro Aso serves as supreme adviser. US Ambassador Glass attended the inaugural meeting and cited Trump's post-summit call to Takaichi as evidence of strong US-Japan ties. Critics drew comparisons to former factional structures.

stories.headline: BOJ Governor Ueda meets Takaichi; no June rate hike discussed, coordination pledged
stories.summary: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda met with PM Takaichi on May 22 to exchange views on monetary policy. Ueda said no specific discussion of a June rate hike took place and both sides agreed to maintain close communication. Takaichi's aides have publicly questioned the timing of BOJ rate hikes given ongoing energy-driven inflation; US Treasury Secretary Bessent separately tweeted a warning to Ueda about forex intervention.

stories.headline: Japan April core inflation falls to four-year low as energy subsidies take effect; BOJ rate path uncertain
stories.summary: Japan's core inflation slowed to a four-year low in April, driven by government fuel and education subsidies, complicating the BOJ's case for a near-term rate hike. Export data for April also beat expectations, rising for an eighth consecutive month despite Middle East supply disruptions. Governor Ueda's June 3 speech is flagged as the next key signal on rate direction.

stories.headline: Japan-South Korea ties deepen with energy pact and sixth Takaichi-Lee summit in Andong
stories.summary: PM Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung held their sixth summit in under a year in Andong, South Korea on May 19, agreeing to bolster energy cooperation amid Middle East instability. Analysis pieces note the unlikely chemistry between the conservative Takaichi and progressive Lee as potentially heralding a new era in bilateral relations, despite persistent differences on North Korea policy.

stories.headline: LDP drafts security document revision calling for interceptor drones and year-long combat sustainability
stories.summary: Japan's LDP formally drafted proposals to revise the country's three key security documents, calling for early deployment of interceptor drones, high-energy weapons, next-generation submarines for counterstrike missions, and the capacity to sustain combat for at least one year. The draft stops short of specifying defense spending targets. The LDP plans to finalize proposals in early June.

stories.headline: Philippine President Marcos to make state visit to Japan, meet Takaichi and Emperor Naruhito
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is scheduled to visit Japan from Tuesday for a state visit including meetings with PM Takaichi and Emperor Naruhito. He will receive the Grand Cordon of the Supreme Order of the Chrysanthemum. Security cooperation, maritime security, and energy development are expected to be central topics given the China-related tensions in the region.

stories.headline: Albanian PM Rama visits Tokyo; Takaichi expresses support for Albania's EU accession
stories.summary: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama was received with an official ceremony by PM Takaichi in Tokyo on May 22. Takaichi voiced Japan's full support for Albania's EU membership and highlighted shared values, while Rama discussed Indo-Pacific cooperation and invited Takaichi to Albania for next year's NATO summit. Coverage spanned Albanian, Italian, and Japanese outlets.

stories.headline: Takaichi announces investment quota for 17 growth sectors including AI and semiconductors
stories.summary: At a May 22 meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy — which Takaichi chairs — she outlined plans to create a dedicated investment quota exempting 17 growth sectors including AI, semiconductors, and finance from regular budget constraints. Social security reform and insurance premium reduction targets were also discussed.

stories.headline: Emperor Naruhito holds multiple ceremonial engagements; UN Secretary-General audience in Tokyo
stories.summary: Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako undertook several public engagements this week, including hosting the UN Secretary-General for an audience in Tokyo, attending the 76th National Tree Planting Festival in Ehime, attending the JAID 100th anniversary ceremony, and Princess Aiko representing the imperial family at the Laos Festival in Yoyogi Park. The Emperor also hosted Australian business figures receiving the Order of the Rising Sun. A Dutch royal event mentioned Emperor Naruhito's upcoming state visit to the Netherlands around the World Cup.

stories.headline: LDP, Nippon Ishin, and DPP push emergency constitutional clause; My Number card mandatory proposal also advanced
stories.summary: Three parties — the LDP, Japan Innovation Party (Nippon Ishin), and the Democratic Party for the People — voiced support Sunday for an emergency clause in Japan's constitution to handle governance during a crisis coinciding with an election. The same week, the LDP's Digital Society Promotion Headquarters proposed making My Number national ID card ownership mandatory, with no penalty for noncompliance.

stories.headline: Japan passes joint child custody reform ending 80-year sole-custody system
stories.summary: Japan's House of Councillors passed a reform to allow joint custody for divorced parents, ending a sole-custody system that had been in place for approximately 80 years. The bill passed with cross-party support including LDP, Komeito, CDP, Nippon Ishin, and DPP, though judges retain authority to block shared custody in cases of abuse or harm to children.

articles.title: Japan approves joint custody for divorced parents after 80 years

stories.headline: Team Mirai leader calls himself Takaichi's 'AI tutor' at first party leaders' debate
stories.summary: At the first party leaders' debate in the Diet on May 20, Team Mirai leader Takahiro Anno offered to serve as PM Takaichi's AI tutor, arguing that AI's impact on society would rival the Industrial Revolution and urging Takaichi to personally experience the latest AI tools. The exchange received coverage in Japan Forward in both English and Japanese.

stories.summary: Japan's Keidanren (Japan Business Federation) released its fourth annual Startup Friendly Scoring of major Japanese companies, with Dentsu Group taking second place for the third consecutive year and NEC ranking fifth. A Spanish-language op-ed from Ecuador separately noted an upcoming Keidanren visit to Ecuador in July, describing significant interest from Japanese executives in the market.
